relationship: Logitech dollar sales as the unit driver of Nordic's chips
evidence: price lifted Logitech's gross margin 1.5 pts (Q2 FY26 call) = a price step of 2.8% of sales, in YoY from 2025Q2 to early 2026Q2; Americas sell-in -4.9% / -3.6% (2025Q2/Q3) while group sales grew and sell-through ran ahead ('lower demand early in the quarter as a result of the pricing actions')
treatment: new: the unit driver removes the price step (2.8 pts at most). Logitech's own dollar forecast needs no change; Nordic's chain term (weight 0 at h=1) moves by well under 1m

relationship: Nordic consumer on Logitech sell-through (t-2), across the price step
dated_by: first Nordic quarter whose t-2 driver carries the step
evidence: Chow: p 0.776 on the dollar driver, 0.909 on the unit driver; n 15 / 3 (too few quarters after the step to have power)
treatment: reported; no slope re-estimated on three quarters

relationship: timing of Logitech's purchases (chip orders to ODMs)
dated_by: purchases pulled in ahead of new tariffs (Q2 FY26 call)
evidence: Logitech inventory 81 days in 2025Q1 vs 71 a year earlier; back to 69 in 2025Q2
treatment: no change to the lags; a one-quarter pull-forward, reversed in 2025Q2. Production moved out of China for US (<10% by Dec 2025): lag change not measurable

relationship: end demand vs the channel in Nordic's 2022-24 fall
evidence: 2023: Nordic consumer -38% YoY, of which the Logitech+GN slice -3.2 pts and the rest of Nordic -34 pts; top-10 customers -3% vs broad market -46% (2023). Link at 2024Q2: Chow F 0.27 (p 0.766); HAC Wald p 0.606; slope +1.66 before, +1.07 after; n 9 / 9
treatment: end demand enters through the driver; the fall of 2023 is the channel (building / destock state), not a new relationship

relationship: industry sales (WSTS) as a proxy for Nordic's market
dated_by: AI data-centre spending (May 2023 guidance shock); dated with the data in view
evidence: corr(WSTS YoY, Nordic YoY) +0.67 before (n 10) vs +0.27 after (n 12), Fisher-z p 0.29; Chow p 0.115; WSTS +129% in 2026Q2 vs Nordic +33%
treatment: WSTS / SIA are context only, never a regressor (Pipeline B)

relationship: distributor dollars as a proxy for peripherals demand
dated_by: memory price surge; dated with the data in view
evidence: TD Synnex minus Logitech sales YoY: -0.0 pts on average from 2023Q1 (n 11, sd 9.6), +12.8 after (n 3: +4, +11, +24), Welch t 1.9 (p 0.15); rising each quarter; TD Synnex +38% in 2026Q3;
treatment: distributor dollars are not a driver; ASP tailwind removed (config structural_breaks); the TD Synnex light is context only

relationship: the channel-cycle signal (Microchip MCU distributor days)
evidence: Microchip distributor days 28, 26, 25 since then: no memory or AI inflation in the MCU channel
treatment: the cycle state keeps its signal

relationship: Nordic revenue = demand (vs = supply, as in 2021-22)
evidence: CEO: 'It hasn't limited us yet, but it's very tight. It's running at its almost maximum pace.' nRF54 / nRF5340 lead time 16 weeks
treatment: watched: lead time above 20 weeks or stock down 50% (monitoring plan W4); if it binds, the 2021-22 treatment applies
